title: CS Signal Hub & Scope Synthesizer — first-pass aggregation for enterprise asks
creator: Anika Shah
description:
Problem: Sales and CS surface a high volume of enterprise feature asks that arrive as freeform emails, Slack threads, and CRM tickets. The downstream PM/ENG triage work is manual, inconsistent, and frequently misses reuse opportunities across accounts. Goal: build a lightweight 'CS Signal Hub' and a 'Scope Synthesizer' workflow that automatically aggregates enterprise asks, normalizes fields, and produces a first-pass scoping bundle for PM review. The output should reduce PM review time per request and surface repeatable feature patterns for batching and prioritization.

Scope: ingest Sales/CS forms, Zendesk/HubSpot exports, and a curated Slack channel. Normalize attributes (customer, ARR bucket, use-case, success metric, regulatory sensitivity, requested SLA). Run a rules-based scorer (customer value x implementation complexity heuristic) to assign a priority band and suggest a draft scope (MVP surface, constrained success criteria). Export results to Linear (ticket draft) + Confluence summary + CSV for PM review.

Out of scope: fully automated acceptance/release decisions, backend implementation of features, or replacing existing enterprise intake playbooks — this is an assistive synthesis layer for PMs and CS reps.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest pipeline accepts CSV/JSON export from HubSpot/Zendesk and messages from a dedicated #cs-enterprise-requests Slack channel
Normalization step maps incoming text to standard fields: customer_name, ARR_tier, use_case_category, requested_workflow, compliance_flag
Scope Synthesizer outputs a one-paragraph draft scope + 3 bullet success criteria and an estimated effort bucket (S/M/L) for each request
System assigns a priority band (P0/P1/P2) using configurable weights and stores rationale in the draft ticket
PMs can review and convert synthesized drafts into canonical Linear tickets with a single click, preserving source links
Automated deduplication groups >70% of clearly-duplicate asks from the same account or identical text templates
Metrics dashboard shows ingestion volume, synth accuracy (PM accepted vs edited), and time-to-first-draft reduced by >=50% vs manual baseline
milestones: 2025-03-04: basic ingest prototype (CSV + Slack) live in staging
2025-03-18: Scope Synthesizer v1 (rules + heuristics) + Linear draft export
2025-04-01: evaluate pilot, iterate, decide go/no-go for org rollout
decisions: Use a rules-first approach for v1 (no ML model training) to enable explainability for PM/CS reviewers — agreed 2025-02-18
Normalize ARR tiers into three buckets (SMB/Scale/Enterprise) and use ARR weight multiplier for priority scoring
Flag compliance/regulatory keywords at ingest and force security_review_required=true for any match
Export canonical draft to Linear as unassigned ticket with source traceability and 'synth_score' metadata
work_log: 2025-02-15 — Kickoff: aligned stakeholders (PM, CS ops, Eng infra, Design). Assigned data ownership to CS ops.
2025-02-21 — Field taxonomy workshop: finalized list of 12 normalized fields and mapped common HubSpot properties. Action: DES to produce form UI mockups.
2025-02-27 — ENG prototype: created ingest lambda for CSV + Slack relay; basic parsing and mapping present. Open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/enterprisedata/pull/52
2025-03-02 — PM review: early synth outputs inconsistent on scope length. Decided to enforce 1 paragraph + 3 bullets; updated synthesizer template.

2025-03-04 — Staging deploy: pipeline connected to staging Slack and a sample HubSpot export. Initial dedupe heuristic in place; false-positive rate ~18% on sample set. Filing follow-up ENG task ENG-4038 to refine fuzzy matching.
next_steps: ENG: complete fuzzy-dedupe improvements (ENG-4038) and reduce false positives to <10%
DES: publish form and Linear draft UI (DES-1308) for CS pilot intake flow
PM: schedule pilot kickoff with three AE pods for 2025-03-25 and prepare success metrics
CS Ops: nominate point-of-contact and supply a month of anonymized exports for training heuristics
